data.name: Crongdor the Barbarian
data.detailed_description:
In a time before time, out of the mist-cloaked North came the barbarians!
Come to pillage the shadow-haunted temples of the wicked cults of civilisation.
The barbarians were grim, brutal men, with thickly corded muscles.
They spoke in a barking tongue, and were proficient with long sword and javelin.

Let me tell you the tale of the strongest and most valiant of the barbarians.
His name made the mightiest tyrants quake on their thrones.
This is the tale of Crongdor - barbarian, raider, thief!

Features


  • Lop off heads, skewer with javelins, and furiously hammer your way through 8 hectic temples.
  • Heavy metal theme music from Hornanvasara!
  • Entire physics module written for bouncing, rolling decapitated heads.
  • Survive dart traps, crushing boulders, and warlock ambushes.
  • Topple temple pillars like dominoes with your god-gifted maul.
  • Extremely difficult - only true barbarians need apply.
  • Wipe the guts off your screen!
  • Game progression is casual - an attempt to unlock the next temple takes a few minutes ... but you may need many, many attempts.
  • Make your own custom maps full of traps and secrets using our map editor.
  • Full C++ / OpenGL source code package.

Mods and Source Code


We are very happy to help you pull the game apart and explain how it was made, and what some of the lessons learned, design decisions, and insights from the project were. If you're interested in programming games from the ground up in C or C++, distributing for multiple platforms, or programming OpenGL computer graphics, or just curious about how the "guts" of these things look, then you will enjoy following along and chatting with us. We will most likely try a combination of written, video, stream, and forum content. We've kept the game really easy to mod, so if you want to replace the art, make new enemies or maps you can do so. You will of course have access to the source code, warts and all, so you can see how it was done and modify it.

reviews.review:
Developed by Anton Gerdelan and published by Ripped Wizards, Crongdor the Barbarian is an indie action title that proudly embraces the spirit of classic arcade-inspired hack-and-slash games. Rather than focusing on cinematic storytelling or complex role-playing mechanics, it delivers a straightforward adventure centered on surviving deadly temples packed with enemies, traps, and hazards. You step into the role of Crongdor, a fierce barbarian whose journey revolves around battling relentless foes while navigating dangerous ruins where every room presents a new challenge. Its premise is simple, but that simplicity allows the game to concentrate almost entirely on fast, satisfying action that rewards skill and persistence.

Combat is the heart of the experience, emphasizing quick reactions and careful positioning over button-mashing. Crongdor has access to a variety of brutal attacks, including melee strikes, thrown javelins, and a massive hammer capable of destroying environmental objects and crushing enemies in spectacular fashion. The game's physics system plays a surprisingly important role, allowing players to interact with pillars, debris, and even enemy remains in entertaining ways. The exaggerated violence is intentionally humorous rather than realistic, creating a tone that feels like an affectionate tribute to old fantasy action games. Every battle becomes a balance between aggressive offense and cautious movement, particularly when multiple enemies attack alongside deadly environmental hazards.

The temples themselves provide much of the game's challenge. Each stage introduces traps such as poison darts, collapsing obstacles, rolling boulders, and hostile spellcasters that require players to stay alert at all times. The difficulty is intentionally high, encouraging repeated attempts as players gradually memorize layouts and improve their combat skills. Success depends far more on player mastery than on character upgrades, giving every victory a satisfying sense of accomplishment. While the demanding nature of the gameplay may discourage players looking for a more relaxed adventure, those who enjoy overcoming difficult obstacles through practice will likely appreciate the rewarding progression.

One of the game's most distinctive strengths lies outside its gameplay. Crongdor the Barbarian includes a complete map editor that allows players to design their own temples filled with enemies, traps, and custom challenges. Even more impressive is the inclusion of the game's complete C++ and OpenGL source code, giving aspiring developers a rare opportunity to examine how the game was built. This level of openness is uncommon in commercial releases and significantly extends the value of the package, transforming it into both an entertaining game and an educational resource for anyone interested in programming or game development.

Visually, the game favors clear, functional presentation over cutting-edge graphics. The environments are designed to keep hazards and enemies easy to recognize during hectic encounters, while the fantasy aesthetic complements the barbarian theme without becoming overly elaborate. The heavy metal soundtrack further reinforces the energetic atmosphere, adding intensity to battles and helping establish the game's rugged personality. Although it lacks the visual polish of larger-budget productions, its artistic choices remain consistent with its old-school design philosophy and contribute to its unique charm.

Crongdor the Barbarian succeeds because it never loses sight of what it wants to be. It delivers challenging action, creative environmental combat, and rewarding gameplay built around skill rather than progression systems. The addition of extensive creation tools and full source code makes it stand out from many indie action games, offering value beyond the main campaign. Players seeking a story-driven or highly accessible experience may find its uncompromising difficulty too demanding, but fans of classic hack-and-slash games with a taste for challenging gameplay and developer transparency will discover a memorable and worthwhile adventure.

Rating: 6/10
